title: NetDiff: Graph Diffusion with Improved Global Capabilities to Generate and Update Mobile Network Topologies
claim: Given a set of unconnected nodes, the task is to assign a consistent link topology and role labeling.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, large arrow from unlinked to linked nodes
description: The figure has two halves joined by a long black arrow pointing right. On the left, ten grey airplane icons are scattered at different orientations, each with a thin line across the wings, and none are connected. On the right, the same airplanes appear in the same layout, now colored red or blue. Black double-headed arrows link pairs of planes, forming a sparse network. The red and blue colors mark the two transmit/receive parity classes. Links mostly join planes of opposite colors. The eye goes first to the colored planes on the right, then back along the arrow to the grey planes on the left. There is no text, no math and no legend. The airplanes stand in for nodes with sectorized antennas.
caption: Our system consists of flying nodes equipped with sectorized antennas. We want to assign them a topology of links and a matching emission-reception parity to determine in which time slot they can emit.
abstract: We introduce NetDiff, a node-conditioned denoising diffusion model that generates directional link topologies and a two-slot transmit/receive parity for mobile ad hoc networks. Directional antennas can yield high throughput but require globally consistent link decisions under sector, interference, connectivity, and half-duplex constraints. NetDiff improves global coherence with Absolute Cross-Attentive Modulation (ACAM) tokens, which provide permutation-invariant global signals and help the model match graph-level counts (e.g., density and sector usage). We also propose partial diffusion to update an existing topology with a small number of denoising steps, enabling fast reconfiguration under mobility. NetDiff reaches over 95 % of target performance with constant inference time, outperforms heuristic and omnidirectional baselines, and improves over a strong diffusion graph-transformer baseline in key metrics.
